transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is my eating’s been really off. Some days before a shift I barely manage coffee and maybe a granola bar, and that’s kind of it. My scrubs have been hanging loose lately too, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your appetite or experienced unintentional weight loss recently?

Yeah. My appetite’s definitely been down. Some days before work I only get down coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I just don’t feel like eating much. And I’ve noticed my scrubs are fitting looser, even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you found yourself avoiding eating certain foods or changing your eating habits out of a fear of gaining weight or because of a strong desire to be thinner?

No, it’s not really about wanting to be thinner or worrying about gaining weight. My eating’s just been off — like before a shift I might only manage coffee and a granola bar, and that’s it. And my scrubs are getting loose, but I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you been feeling unusually sad, anxious, or stressed around the times when you're not eating well?
Yeah… sad, mostly. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, like the day’s already gone bad before I even get my badge on. When I feel like that, eating just doesn’t really happen.
Do you feel depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah… I do. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put my badge on. It sticks with me a lot of the day.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with people?

Yeah, I have. I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, play chess with friends… stuff like that. Lately I just tell myself there’s no point, and I end up sitting at home scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet instead.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been physically active?
Yeah. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, I wake up feeling like I already worked a double shift. By lunchtime I’m usually dragging and trying hard just to keep my thoughts together.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much lately?

Yeah. I have trouble sleeping through the night. I’ll lie there replaying stuff from work and listening for noises, and then I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. After that I can’t really settle back down before the alarm goes off.
How long have you been feeling this way — with the sadness, loss of interest, fatigue, and trouble eating and sleeping?
It’s been a while now. The more steady depression and not caring about things really settled in later, but I’d say it’s been going on for about a year and four months.
Have your feelings of sadness, fatigue, and loss of interest made it significantly harder for you to do your job, be around people, or take care of things in your daily life?

Yes. It’s been affecting me pretty clearly. At work I’ve started making mistakes I shouldn’t be making, simple stuff, and I have to ask coworkers to repeat things they just told me. Outside of work I’ve been avoiding chess nights and photography walks because I don’t really trust myself to keep up or act normal around people.
Have you often woken up earlier than you intended in the mornings, even when you haven’t set an alarm?

Yes, pretty often. Even if I’m not trying to get up early, I’ll wake around 3 or 4 and then I just can’t really settle back down. I’m usually lying there thinking about work or listening for noises until the alarm would go off anyway.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough, or been overwhelmed by guilt, even when you haven't done anything particularly wrong?

Yes. I keep feeling like I’m more trouble than help, especially at the clinic. If I make some small mistake, like taking too long to turn over a room, I’ll blame myself like I’ve messed up everyone’s whole day. And at home I get the same feeling, like I’m just a burden to my family.
Have you ever had a period in the past when you felt this way for more than two weeks in a row?

Yes. This kind of feeling has lasted more than a couple weeks before. I get stuck thinking I’m a burden to people at the clinic and to my family, and if I make some small mistake, like slowing down a room turnover, I blame myself like I’ve ruined everyone’s day.
